item.title: Inflation climbs in India, Greece, and France as energy costs surge
item.description: Fresh data released this week showed inflation accelerated in India, Greece, and France during March, with rising energy and food prices fanning price pressures across three continents amid the fallout from the conflict in the Middle East.

item.title: MIT quantum sensor measures multiple properties at once
item.description: Researchers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology have developed a quantum sensor capable of measuring several physical properties simultaneously, overcoming a long-standing limitation of solid-state sensors that has confined them to reading only one quantity at a time.

item.title: AMD, Arm, and Qualcomm invest $60M in self-driving startup Wayve
item.description:
Three of the world's largest chipmakers have joined forces to back Wayve, the London-based autonomous driving startup, investing a combined $60 million as part of an extension to its Series D funding round. AMD, Arm, and Qualcomm Ventures announced the investment on Wednesday, deepening the semiconductor industry's bet on a software-first approach to self-driving cars.

The deal means Wayve now counts all four major automotive chip suppliers — including Nvidia, which invested in the original round — among its shareholders, giving the startup relationships across essentially every compute platform an automaker might use.

item.title: US and Iran both deny reported ceasefire extension deal
item.description: Mediators working to salvage the fragile US-Iran ceasefire said Wednesday that both sides have reached an "in principle agreement" to extend the truce beyond its April 22 expiration, according to regional officials cited by the Associated Press. The reported breakthrough, however, was swiftly denied by both Washington and Tehran, leaving the diplomatic picture murky as back-channel negotiations continue through Pakistan.

item.title: Europe accelerates 'European NATO' plan as Trump threatens to quit alliance
item.description: European nations are accelerating a contingency plan to defend the continent using NATO's existing military structures should the United States scale back its role in the alliance, according to an exclusive report by The Wall Street Journal published on Monday. The effort, informally referred to as a "European NATO," marks a turning point in transatlantic relations strained by President Donald Trump's repeated threats to withdraw from the 77-year-old alliance.

item.title: BBC to cut up to 2,000 jobs in sweeping overhaul
item.description: The BBC is planning to cut up to 2,000 jobs across its departments, amounting to roughly one in 10 of its workforce, in one of the most far-reaching restructuring efforts in the broadcaster's recent history. Staff are expected to be briefed on the scale of the reductions at an all-staff meeting on Tuesday, according to the Financial Times.

item.title: Iran warns U.S. naval blockade could unravel ceasefire as energy crisis accelerates EV shift
item.description:
The war between the United States, Israel, and Iran — now in its seventh week — has triggered a global energy shock that is accelerating the world's pivot toward renewable power and electric vehicles, even as a fragile ceasefire and fresh U.S. naval blockade keep oil markets on edge.

Since the conflict began on February 28, the closure of the Strait of Hormuz has choked off roughly one-fifth of global oil and gas trade, sending Brent crude surging more than 60 percent in March alone, the largest monthly jump since the 1980s. Although a two-week ceasefire brokered on April 8 brought prices down sharply, oil remains roughly 30 percent above pre-war levels, and Iran warned on Wednesday that the newly enforced U.S. naval blockade of its ports could unravel the truce. The Associated Press reported that a Pakistani delegation arrived in Tehran on Wednesday to arrange a possible second round of U.S.-Iran talks.

item.title: Cadence taps Google's Gemini to power AI chip design agent
item.description:
Cadence Design Systems announced a collaboration with Google on Tuesday to optimize its ChipStack AI Super Agent with Gemini on Google Cloud, the latest in a series of partnerships aimed at embedding artificial intelligence across the semiconductor design process. The announcement, made as the company kicked off its CadenceLIVE Silicon Valley conference, builds on an expanded collaboration with Nvidia first revealed in March.

The Google partnership pairs Cadence's agentic chip design platform with Google's Gemini large language models, hosted on Google Cloud infrastructure. The goal is to improve the accuracy of AI-generated outputs for chip design tasks, with Google Cloud providing the compute needed to run Gemini alongside Cadence's electronic design automation tools. The ChipStack AI Super Agent is now available through the Google Cloud Marketplace.

"By merging ChipStack AI Agent with Gemini, we are propelling forward the evolution of intelligent design — leveraging the reasoning capabilities of large language models alongside Cadence's premier EDA engines," said Paul Cunningham, Cadence's senior vice president and general manager.

item.title: NASA says 'god of chaos' asteroid will be visible to the naked eye in 2029
item.description: Three years from now, on April 13, 2029, asteroid 99942 Apophis — named after the Egyptian deity of chaos — will pass within about 20,000 miles (32,000 kilometers) of Earth's surface, closer than satellites in geosynchronous orbit and near enough to be seen with the naked eye from parts of Europe, Africa, and Asia. NASA says the event poses no threat to Earth but will mark one of the closest approaches of an asteroid this size ever recorded.

item.title: Iran offers safe ship passage via Oman side of Hormuz
item.description:
Iran has signaled it could allow ships to sail freely through the Omani side of the Strait of Hormuz without risk of attack, as part of proposals offered in negotiations with the United States aimed at preventing a return to full-scale conflict, according to a Reuters report citing a source briefed by Tehran.

The proposal, reported on Wednesday, comes as a fragile two-week ceasefire — set to expire on April 21 — holds amid escalating pressure from a U.S. naval blockade that has effectively severed Iran's seaborne trade. The offer represents a potential diplomatic off-ramp in a crisis that has caused the largest-ever disruption of global oil and gas supplies, with hundreds of tankers and roughly 20,000 seafarers trapped in the Persian Gulf since the war began on February 28.

item.title: Student kills 9 in Turkey's deadliest school shooting
item.description: A 14-year-old student opened fire at a middle school in southern Turkey on Wednesday, killing nine people and wounding 13 others in the country's deadliest school shooting — and the second such attack in as many days in a nation where such violence had been virtually unknown.

item.title: Chinese tanker turned back at Hormuz as US blockade holds
item.description: A U.S.-sanctioned Chinese-owned tanker that appeared to defy President Trump's naval blockade of Iranian ports has turned back toward the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, according to Reuters, underscoring how the three-day-old blockade is rapidly becoming a flashpoint in U.S.-China relations. The incident involving the Rich Starry — a Malawi-flagged vessel owned by Shanghai Xuanrun Shipping — has stoked fears that any direct American interception of a Chinese-linked ship could trigger a diplomatic crisis weeks before a planned Trump-Xi summit in Beijing.

item.title: IDF chief approves new battle plans for Iran and Lebanon
item.description: Israel's military Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir announced Wednesday that he has approved updated battle plans for continued operations against both Hezbollah in Lebanon and Iran, declaring Israeli forces prepared for immediate action. The announcement came during a visit to troops in southern Lebanon and coincided with the first direct Israeli-Lebanese talks in over three decades in Washington.

item.title: CENTCOM says Iran naval blockade 'fully implemented' after 48 hours
item.description:
The U.S. military said Wednesday that ten vessels had complied with orders to turn around and return toward Iranian ports or coastal areas during the first 48 hours of a naval blockade, as Washington moved to choke off Tehran's maritime trade amid the ongoing war.

"No vessels have made it past US forces," U.S. Central Command said in a statement posted on X, declaring the blockade "fully implemented" after just 36 hours. CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper said U.S. forces had "completely halted economic trade going in and out of Iran by sea," noting that roughly 90 percent of Iran's economy depends on international maritime commerce.

item.title: Bukele enacts life sentences for minors as young as 12
item.description: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele has signed into law sweeping legal reforms allowing life imprisonment for minors as young as 12 convicted of homicide, terrorism, or rape, according to the country's official gazette as reported by Reuters. The measures, published on Wednesday and scheduled to take effect on April 26, mark one of the harshest juvenile sentencing regimes in the world.

item.title: Hezbollah fires 30+ rockets at northern Israel amid stalled diplomacy
item.description: Hezbollah launched a wave of rocket and drone strikes against Israeli targets on Wednesday, hitting settlements and military positions across northern Israel even as diplomatic efforts between Beirut and Jerusalem showed few signs of progress. The day's attacks triggered air-raid sirens across Kiryat Shmona, the Galilee panhandle, and western Galilee communities, marking another sharp escalation in a conflict that has raged since early March.

item.title: Israel's security cabinet to weigh Lebanon ceasefire
item.description:
Israel's security cabinet is set to convene Wednesday evening to discuss a possible ceasefire in Lebanon, according to a senior Israeli official who spoke to Reuters, a development that follows the first direct diplomatic engagement between Israel and Lebanon in more than three decades.

The cabinet meeting, scheduled for 8 p.m. local time, comes one day after Israeli and Lebanese ambassadors met at the U.S. State Department in Washington for over two hours of talks hosted by Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The trilateral meeting — which included Israeli Ambassador Yechiel Leiter and Lebanese Ambassador Nada Hamadeh Moawad — concluded with all sides agreeing to "launch direct negotiations at a mutually agreed time and venue," according to a State Department statement.

item.title: US insists Lebanon, Iran peace talks stay on separate tracks
item.description:
The Trump administration has made clear that any peace deal between Israel and Lebanon must be negotiated independently of the ongoing U.S.-Iran nuclear talks, a deliberate decoupling designed to deny Tehran leverage over the pace of diplomacy on either front.

A senior U.S. official told Axios that Washington has not asked Israel for a ceasefire in Lebanon, and that the Lebanon track is not part of the peace negotiations with Iran. The official added that President Donald Trump would "welcome and be happy with an end of hostilities" as part of an agreement reached directly between Israel and Lebanon.

item.title: Brazil's ex-spy chief freed from ICE custody in US
item.description:
Former Brazilian intelligence chief Alexandre Ramagem was released from U.S. immigration custody on Wednesday, just two days after being detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement in Orlando, Florida, according to Reuters. His release was announced by Bolsonaro ally Paulo Figueiredo on the social media platform X, writing "Alexandre Ramagem is free," while Ramagem's name was also removed from ICE's online detainee database.

ICE did not respond to inquiries about the release, and Reuters reported it was unable to determine Ramagem's current immigration status in the United States.

item.title: 'Bathtub ring' on Mars offers best evidence yet of ancient ocean
item.description:
A vast ocean may have once lapped against the shores of Mars for millions of years, according to a study published Wednesday in the journal Nature that identifies a geological formation on the Red Planet strikingly similar to the continental shelves found along Earth's coastlines.

Researchers Abdallah Zaki, a postdoctoral scholar at the University of Texas at Austin, and Michael Lamb, a professor of geology at Caltech, found a wide, flat band of terrain wrapping the boundary between Mars's northern lowlands and southern highlands — a feature they liken to the ring left around a drained bathtub. The ocean it implies would have covered roughly a third of the planet's surface.
